title: Habit Portfolio — Quarterly Check & OKR Draft
content:
Purpose: quick, product-style check on personal habits + OKR targets. Treat habits like a small investment portfolio — rebalance quarterly.

Context and framing
- Goal: move from ad-hoc "do-more" energy to a durable set of behaviors that directly move my core work metrics (time to unblock, weekly PR throughput, energy for deep work).
- Quarter focus: stabilize a repeatable review cadence, surface signal (not noise), and run 2 small experiments that reduce context-switching.
- Why portfolio metaphor: I want to think in weights (effort allocation), not in single goals. Some habits are long-term (compounding), some are runway/hacks.

Current habit portfolio (weights are subjective: high/med/low):
- Deep prime (90-min focused blocks twice a week) — high
- Meeting triage ritual (15 min daily morning email + 1p Slack status) — med
- PR batching (group reviews into 2 slots/day) — med
- Health buffer (run or gym 3x/week) — low
- Learning slot (30 min, reading distill/benchmarks) — low

Quarterly OKR draft (for personal tracking, not team OKRs):
- Objective: Increase reliable deep-work output to unblock product experiments and lower lead time.
  - KR1: Reduce median time from "blocked" flag to unblocked PR to <= 24h for my ownership bugs. (baseline: ~38h)
  - KR2: Ship 6 small experiments (canary config changes, batching heuristics, alert tweaks) with measurable delta in latency or on-call noise. Target: 6/6 with at least 1 positive delta >5%
  - KR3: Maintain 80% completion of scheduled deep-prime blocks (target: 80% of planned sessions completed)

Signal definitions / instrumentation notes
- "Blocked" tracking: use Jira label personal-block and a small spreadsheet quick log for now (columns: date, ticket, blocker, time-resolved).
- Ship count: PR merged + feature flag toggled. Tag PRs with `habit-experiment` label.
- Deep-prime completion: calendar event with private tag -> cross-check after week. If >20% misses, analyze cause.

Weekly check-in template (2–3 bullet minutes, keep sharp)
- Wins this week (what shipped or unblocked)
- Signals: any change in time-to-unblock, latency, noise (quantitative if possible)
- Stuck: 1 thing blocking next week + next action
- Rebalance note: did I shift weight between habits? yes/no + reason

Sample weekly entry (scratch):
- 2026-03-09
  - Wins: landed PR #331 (auto-batcher fallback) -> reduced tail latency by ~6% in staging.
  - Signals: my "blocked" log shows 3 items resolved within 18h (improved).
  - Stuck: waiting on infra quota for canary rollout (ENG-4821) -> next action: ping infra with concrete window (Mon 9–11).
  - Rebalance: increased batching focus; lowered reading time this week.

Small experiments (ideas and quick success criteria)
- Experiment A: passive calendar snooze for meeting invites (auto-decline >30m meetings in deep-prime windows). Success: reclaim 1.5h/week and keep deep-prime completion >=80%
- Experiment B: 24h "quick triage" SLA for tickets labeled personal-block. Success: drop median unblock time by >=20%
- Experiment C: temporary 48h PR batching (review windows only at 10:00 and 16:00). Success: no adverse latency in reviews; improved context retention (self-reported).

Retrospective prompts (end of quarter)
- Which habits had compounding effects (3+ weeks of downstream improvement)?
- Which habits felt like overhead and should be retired?
- Were KRs set at the right ambition level?
- What are three micro-commitments to carry into the next quarter?

Open questions / risks
- How to measure "quality of focus" without adding heavy instrumentation? (simple proxy: % of calendar time in focused events + count of interruptions logged)
- Risk of over-optimizing on speed (unblock time) and harming long-term design. Mitigation: pair unblock KR with one quality anchor (post-ship review).

Immediate next actions (today/this week)
- Create `personal-block` quick filter in Jira and add initial backlog (10 recent examples). (ETA: Wed)
- Add `habit-experiment` label to our dev-examples repo and open a stub PR template. (ETA: Fri)
- Schedule deep-prime slots for the next two weeks and mark auto-decline rule for calendars. (ETA: Mon)

Notes to self (bite-sized reminders)
- It's OK to fail experiments; track them as data.
- Rebalancing is not abandonment — swap low-value habits for higher-leverage ones.
- Keep weekly check-ins <=7 min; this is about signal, not therapy.

References and quick links
- Confluence: habit portfolio primer (linked artifact)
- Jira: ENG-4821 (infra quota blocking canary)
- PR template idea: link in linked_artifacts to PR #88

Bottom line (one-sentence): Treat personal habits like a tiny product portfolio — measure the signals, run short experiments, and rebalance quarterly so that deep work reliably produces unblock and shipped experiments.
